name: Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment-I (SAFFIRE-I)
platform: Cygnus OA-6 Cargo Resupply Spacecraft (S.S. Rick Husband)
facility: Saffire Flow Duct and Avionics Module
lead_investigators: David L. Urban (NASA GRC, Project Manager)
Gary A. Ruff (NASA GRC, Project Scientist)
James S. T'ien (Case Western Reserve University)
description: SAFFIRE-I was the first large-scale intentional fire experiment conducted aboard an uncrewed spacecraft (Orbital ATK Cygnus OA-6) after de-berthing from the ISS. It evaluated realistic flame growth, spread rate, temperature fields, and toxic gas release across a 0.4 m wide by 0.94 m long fabric sample in microgravity under controlled forced air flow, breaking prior safety limitations of small-scale laboratory testing in crewed compartments.
gravity_regime: Microgravity (~10^-5 g to 10^-4 g on orbit)
apparatus: Flow duct unit (1.3 m total length, 0.5 x 0.5 m cross section) with flow straighteners, electric hot-wire igniter, calibrated flow fan (~20 cm/s), 29 thermocouples, narrow-angle & wide-angle radiometers, pressure transducers, O2/CO2 sensors, and high-resolution video cameras.
fuels_tested: SIBAL cloth (75% cotton / 25% fiberglass by weight, surface density ~18 mg/cm2)
test_dimensions: 0.40 m width x 0.94 m length x 0.32 mm thickness

experimental_conditions.initial_atmosphere: Cabin air (approx. 21% O2, balance N2, 101.3 kPa)
